scope: Primary literature and previously pinned solver-source evidence relevant to exact adaptive identification trees, response-dependent testing cost, experiment informativeness, and descendant-local pruning.

primary_sources.title: Equivalent Comparisons of Experiments
primary_sources.relevance: Classical comparison of statistical experiments by informativeness. For deterministic experiments, a strict partition refinement is a special case of one experiment being obtainable only by garbling/coarsening another. This special-case connection is a mathematical inference and is not presented as a verbatim theorem statement from the paper.

primary_sources.title: Optimal Binary Identification Procedures
primary_sources.relevance: Establishes the classical finite-hypothesis identification-tree model with object priors, fixed test costs, and dynamic programming for optimal expected testing cost.

primary_sources.title: Diagnosis determination: decision trees optimizing simultaneously worst and expected testing cost
primary_sources.relevance: Shows that simultaneous expected- and worst-cost diagnosis decision trees are an established objective family.

primary_sources.title: Trading off Worst and Expected Cost in Decision Tree Problems and a Value Dependent Model
primary_sources.relevance: Explicitly studies a model where the cost of reading a variable depends on its observed value. Therefore response/value-dependent testing cost is not a Mini-ORIGIN novelty claim.

primary_sources.title: Optimal Decision Tree and Adaptive Submodular Ranking with Noisy Outcomes
primary_sources.relevance: Recent primary reference for the broader ODT literature and noisy/persistent-outcome extensions.

primary_sources.title: Optimal adaptive testing: Informativeness and incentives
primary_sources.relevance: Applies statistical informativeness ordering to adaptive test choice in a strategic model. It is not the same optimization problem, but reinforces that 'choose a more informative test' is established theory rather than a broad novelty claim.

previous_pinned_source_audit.not_found_in_accessible_snapshots: Recomputation of exact response-partition equivalence classes at every descendant state
previous_pinned_source_audit.unresolved_source_gap: MurTree commit 86e439ef537e40cb93afa641aafe2078 could not be obtained reproducibly through the available Bitbucket transport. Its paper is reviewed, but its pinned implementation remains unaudited.

established_not_novel: arbitrary priors and fixed test costs
value/response-dependent testing costs as a problem model
strict deterministic partition refinement as a special case of greater informativeness
the general idea that a more informative no-more-expensive experiment may dominate a coarser one
candidate_contribution_requiring_further: exact descendant-local recomputation of response-partition equivalence classes inside identification-tree dynamic programming
retaining the componentwise Pareto frontier of response-cost vectors inside each local equivalence class
combining that quotient with exact full-diagnosis lower bounds while preserving deterministic lexicographic optimum
the observed exact-search frontier expansion with independent compiled operation-count reproduction
explicitly_not_claimed: novelty of strict partition-refinement dominance in isolation

required_before_publication_novelty_clai: resolve or explicitly retain the MurTree implementation gap
search backward and forward citations of Garey 1972, Cicalese et al. 2014, Saettler et al. 2014, and recent ODT surveys

audit terminology including redundant tests, indistinguishable queries, experiment garbling, Blackwell dominance, partition lattice, sufficient experiments, test subsumption, and state-dependent dominance
obtain review from an outside researcher familiar with optimal decision trees or sequential experimental design
state the contribution narrowly even if no equivalent implementation is found
claim_boundary: This audit narrows claims; it does not prove novelty by absence and is not a scientific performance experiment.
